policy.completion_rule: A domain may set domain_complete=true only when every required capability is exactly 'complete'. 'runtime_pass' is a narrow controlled observation and never closes a domain by itself.
policy.banner_rule: Every domain publishes status_banner verbatim in STATUS.md. The banner is '<title>: INCOMPLETE' while domain_complete is false and '<title>: COMPLETE' only when it is true.
policy.policy_text: A narrow fixture, golden, or single controlled run proves one fact and never closes a domain function. Full stateful completion requires the client/wire path, database persistence, reconnect projection, and the negative paths together. Every handoff must name the next missing behavior for each open domain.

capabilities.title: Backpack open and display
capabilities.notes: The client renders the persisted three-item Backpack as 3/40 with identities 1, 2 and 4 at slots 0, 1 and 3. This is one controlled observation of the projection, not a proof of every bag size, page, or filter.

capabilities.title: Persisted projection survives reconnect
capabilities.notes: Persistence across one merge is runtime-proven. Identity ordering on reconnect is canonicalized client-compatible ordering, not proven original-server policy; see HYP-PF-008 provenance.

capabilities.title: Move any known item to any free slot 0-39
capabilities.notes: Blocked on hypothesis ledger review. The exact client request producer is Grade B proven and an implementation exists as uncommitted work in progress, but HYP-PF-008 accepted_ceiling and stop_rule permit only the single opt-in identity-1 slot-0 to slot-2 composition. Generalizing to any identity and any free slot needs a ledger decision by the project owner before the work may be committed.

capabilities.title: Same-slot move is an exact no-op
capabilities.notes: Blocked behind the same ledger review as move_known_item_any_free_slot. No response, no write and no replay is the intended behavior; it has no runtime evidence yet.

capabilities.title: Negative paths: unknown identity, out-of-range slot, malformed, replay, session and account isolation
capabilities.notes: Offline negative coverage exists for the opt-in composition. Cross-account and cross-session isolation for a generalized move is not covered and has no runtime evidence.

capabilities.title: Occupied destination with a different item: swap, displacement or reject
capabilities.notes: Must remain fail-closed reject until exact original behavior is captured. An explicit reject|swap server parameter defaulting to reject is the planned shape; any swap mode stays Grade D until runtime plus persistence and reconnect evidence exist.

capabilities.title: Compatible stack merge and stack limit behavior
capabilities.notes: One exact V111 merge to quantity 2 is runtime-proven and persisted. The stack ceiling, overflow split-on-merge behavior, and incompatible-template rejection are unproven.

capabilities.title: Split a stack
capabilities.notes: No request producer, response shape, or persistence policy captured.

capabilities.title: Equip and unequip from the Backpack
capabilities.notes: Static boundary between equipped state and the Backpack collection is characterized and one capture exists. No server-side equip operation, persistence, or reconnect projection is implemented.

capabilities.title: Use, drop and sell paths
capabilities.notes: Tracked as separate later milestones. Listed here so the domain can never read as complete while they are missing.

capabilities.title: Every actual server run shows a visible console and mirrors its summary streams
capabilities.notes: One controlled start and requested stop through this exact helper and console host. --self-test-only stays exempt because it opens no listener.

capabilities.title: Requested stop exits server and shim with code 0 and no residue
capabilities.notes: Exactly one stopped marker, zero stderr bytes, zero remaining listeners and processes. Not proof for every signal source.

capabilities.title: Character select, StartGame and scene entry through the real client
capabilities.notes: One single-client session reaching Port Royal with the persisted name projected, then exiting cleanly.

capabilities.title: Session row opens on entry and closes on exit with a durable lease generation
capabilities.notes: Read-only post-state oracle confirms one session row with both timestamps, integrity ok and an empty foreign-key check.

capabilities.title: Abrupt client loss and abrupt server restart recover to a usable state
capabilities.notes: Process-level abrupt loss is covered. Host power loss and storage-level torn writes are not.

capabilities.title: Two or more concurrent clients on separate accounts
capabilities.notes: Every runtime pass so far is single client on one machine. Account isolation, per-session state separation and remote-player projection are unproven.

capabilities.title: Authenticated multi-account access control
capabilities.notes: The local server accepts the development login path only. No credential policy, rate limit, or ownership check is claimed.

capabilities.title: Scene entry places the local player at the persisted position
capabilities.notes: One controlled entry into scene 1 Port Royal at the persisted coordinates with the stable zero-target teleport sent exactly once. This is not proof for any other scene, spawn point, instance, or scene transition.

capabilities.title: Client-reported position is checkpointed and saved on exit
capabilities.notes: The runtime checkpoints the exact client-reported target position and lifecycle.exit saves it, with offline tests covering non-finite rejection and last-writer ordering. The only runtime record shows an unchanged position across an abrupt loss, so a position the player actually moved to surviving reconnect is still unproven.

capabilities.title: Server-side movement validation and authoritative correction
capabilities.notes: Reported positions are accepted as given. No speed, distance, collision, terrain, or line-of-sight validation exists, and no corrective reposition is ever sent. The original server's movement authority model is uncaptured.

capabilities.title: NPC walk and run gait presentation
capabilities.notes: Gait selection is accounted for by the decoded MOBS walk-speed value carried in BasicAttr bit 0x0040, and the accepted rule is that the value must be serialized in every generation and not only the bootstrap, because omitting it from movement snapshots is what turned the observed walk into a run. Observed visually for a fixed set of placements in the legacy scenario runner; it is not a general locomotion or pathing engine. The Foundation population path never requests a movement speed, so no Foundation runtime has reproduced this gait and a test pins that absence.

capabilities.title: Authoritative scene-actor membership and forward/reverse refresh
capabilities.notes: One nearest-20 initial generation plus one forward and one reverse refresh, byte-identical to the frozen V141 builder. Arbitrary scene sizes, streaming under load, and the original server's real population policy are unproven.

capabilities.title: Server-initiated teleport transport
capabilities.notes: One standalone TeleportVital version 4 to a decoded MARKER row transported the client. The TeleportCheck challenge/echo path is only captured, so a server-validated transport with its own acceptance rule does not exist.

capabilities.title: Another player's movement projected to a second client
capabilities.notes: Every runtime pass to date is a single client. No second player has ever been projected, so interest management, update cadence, and interpolation are entirely unknown.

capabilities.title: Hostile relation and target selection
capabilities.notes: One faction value made a scene actor selectable as hostile and the comparator path was traced live. Tab selection alone produced TargetVital without any action, per the V132 negative.

capabilities.title: Client produces a target-bound attack command
capabilities.notes: Double-clicking a hostile actor produced ActionVital 0xEA7D bound to the exact target identity and the same vital reached the server wire in two independent sessions. This proves the request direction only.

capabilities.title: Server acknowledges an action vital
capabilities.notes: The ack is accepted by the client without error, and SCENE-008 traced the consumer as inert: no visible attack, animation, or state change follows. Acknowledgement is not combat.

capabilities.title: Damage application and the server-to-client hit result
capabilities.notes: Blocked on evidence, not on code. A hash-guarded audit proves the curated corpus cannot answer the server-to-client combat-result question, so a new authentic capture is required before any damage number, formula, or result packet may be claimed.

capabilities.title: Knockdown and reaction states
capabilities.notes: The client-side consumer binding is statically characterized and the data-side binding attempt is a recorded negative. Nothing is emitted by the server and no reaction state is stored.

capabilities.title: Skill trigger and skill state
capabilities.notes: Static trigger and hotbar-assignment boundaries exist. No skill is registered, cast, cooled down, or persisted server-side, and no runtime skill use has been observed.

capabilities.title: Behavior lookup and geometric range gating
capabilities.notes: Behavior entry and lookup are traced at runtime and one earlier lookup claim was corrected. The geometric gate call site remains a negative, so no range rule may be asserted.

capabilities.title: HP depletion, death and respawn
capabilities.notes: HP is projected as a static attribute value only. No depletion, death state, corpse, penalty, or respawn path is captured or implemented.

capabilities.title: Monster aggro and server-driven AI
capabilities.notes: Scene actors are projected placements that never react to the player. No aggro radius, threat table, chase, or attack loop exists on the server.

capabilities.title: Player-versus-player engagement rules
capabilities.notes: The client shows a PvP warning dialog during server selection, but no PvP rule, flag, zone, or consequence is implemented or claimed on the server side.

capabilities.title: Character list projection and selection
capabilities.notes: One persisted character was listed and selected through the real client. Multi-character lists, slot ordering, and the classification/faction fields carried in the list are unproven; ARENA-V1 records the classification negative.

capabilities.title: Persisted player name projected into the world view
capabilities.notes: The exact UTF-16LE name field inside ActorAttr rendered above the local player. This closes the local-player name projection only, not remote-player nameboards or name change.

capabilities.title: Create a character through the real client
capabilities.notes: The store implements creation with identity binding, a normalized name key, and a submitted-wire fingerprint, and it is offline-tested. No runtime pass creates a character through the client, and JOB-001 proves no persistent job/class selector has been identified in any wire record, so the creation presets cannot yet be honored.

capabilities.title: Delete a character
capabilities.notes: Only the nested DeleteActorVital record is parsed, deliberately stopping before the outer envelope, dispatch, response, and any repository mutation. The schema carries a soft-delete field. The delete control in the character-select screen must stay unhandled until this is designed, and it must never be exercised during testing.

capabilities.title: Second-password gate
capabilities.notes: An explicit opt-in test-only bypass exists under canonical ledger entry SECOND-PASSWORD-BYPASS-001 and is used by every runtime pass. The authentic verification, storage, and change paths are not implemented; production use stays disallowed.

capabilities.title: Appearance and avatar wire binding
capabilities.notes: Actor and avatar wires are persisted and replayed as opaque bytes with server-side identity rebinding, which preserves appearance without decoding it. No field-level appearance model exists, so appearance cannot be edited, validated, or generated.

capabilities.title: Level, experience and attribute progression
capabilities.notes: The proven projection carries name and cash only. No level, experience, attribute point, or progression rule is modeled, persisted, or captured.

capabilities.title: Server-originated system message
capabilities.notes: ShowMessageVital 0x36D2 carries exactly one wide string and the client renders it in the authentic system panel on the first runtime request. It is emitted by the frozen legacy seam, no Foundation module owns it, and it has no offline test, so it is one observation rather than an owned feature.

capabilities.title: Client chat input reaching the server
capabilities.notes: No chat request produced by typing in the client has been captured, decoded, or dispatched. The request class, command prefixes, and length limits are unknown.

capabilities.title: Channels, whisper and broadcast routing
capabilities.notes: Routing needs at least two concurrent sessions, which no runtime pass has ever established. Channel identifiers and recipient resolution are uncaptured.

capabilities.title: Chat persistence, rate limiting and filtering
capabilities.notes: No chat row exists in the schema and no rate limit or filter is implemented. Listed so the domain can never read as complete while they are missing.

capabilities.title: NPC conversation handshake
capabilities.notes: One click on a placed actor produced TargetVital plus an embedded ChooseNPC, and the server answered with exactly one NPCConversation carrying one descriptor. One actor, one descriptor, one composition.

capabilities.title: Conversation operation and action sequence
capabilities.notes: The operation-1/action-6 then operation-2/action-1 docking-confirm sequence replayed as an exact composition. No semantic name is assigned to the raw operation or action values, and no branching dialogue tree is modeled.

capabilities.title: Quest accept, tracking and completion
capabilities.notes: Three recorded negative boundaries bound where the accept path stops. No quest state is stored server-side, no tracker update is proven, and completion and rewards are untouched.

capabilities.title: Shop browse, buy and sell
capabilities.notes: Captures reach a cash update following a buy. Nothing is implemented in the Foundation store: no shop inventory, no price authority, no transactional buy or sell, and no persistence.

capabilities.title: Interaction negative paths and reachability limits
capabilities.notes: V139 was statically valid but operationally unreachable, and V140 passed only after an explicit synthetic harness position was substituted. That harness is a test device and is never permission to place synthetic positions in production population data.

capabilities.title: Monster spawn cycle and loot
capabilities.notes: Scene actors are static placements. No spawn timer, respawn cycle, drop table, loot object, or pickup path is captured or implemented.
